newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Former Australian diplomat cleared of sex charges.
newsitem.headline: Former Australian diplomat cleared of sex charges.

text.p: A former Australian ambassador accused of having sex with a child in Cambodia was discharged by a court on Wednesday after it ruled there was insufficient evidence for a conviction.
John Holloway, who served as a senior adviser to the Cambodian government after his term as ambassador in the country ended in 1994, had pleaded not guilty.
Canberra Magistrate Michael Somes said there was insufficient evidence for a conviction against Holloway, 53, adding that evidence given by a 16-year-old Cambodian boy was "worthless".
Another Cambodian boy had told a pre-trial committal hearing that Holloway had paid him US$2.00 for anal and oral sex.

Holloway was charged under Australia's child sex tourism laws which allows for Australians to be charged at home over sex offences against children overseas. The law carries a maximum penalty of 17 years in jail.
In April, a Sydney man became the first to be jailed under the new law when he was sentenced to two years for an offence against a girl in the Philippines.

Speaking outside the court, Holloway said the dismissal of the charges raised questions about the law, which he said provided a powerful weapon against Australian officials without providing any protection against false allegations.
Holloway said he looked forward to resuming his career in the Australian foreign service without delay, 18 months after being named in parliament as being a paedophile.
"It has been a black period...," Holloway told reporters.
